claims.text: In PtNi oxygen-reduction catalysts, activity and selectivity are primarily governed by Ni-induced modulation of the d-band center of surface Pt atoms.
An optimized Ni content shifts the Pt d-band center in a way that enhances the binding and conversion of oxygenated intermediates relative to pure Pt.
The performance improvements from optimized Ni alloying are mainly due to electronic modulation rather than strain.
Systematically varying Ni content will tune the d-band center of PtNi catalysts.
Alloying Pt with Ni induces a measurable shift in the d-band center of surface Pt atoms.
Structural characterization can separately quantify or establish the minimal contribution of strain.
Ni alloying changes the electronic structure of surface Pt atoms.
A shift of the surface-Pt d-band center alters adsorption energies for oxygenated ORR intermediates.
The electronic effect caused by Ni alloying enhances ORR catalytic performance.
PtNi catalysts having an optimal Ni content will exhibit enhanced ORR selectivity relative to pure Pt.
PtNi catalysts having an optimal Ni content will exhibit modified ORR activity relative to pure Pt.
A correlation between improved performance and measured d-band-center shifts that persists after controlling for strain would support the proposed mechanism.
The proposed relationship is expected to hold in acidic electrolyte at 25–80 °C when Pt loading and support structure are controlled.
Changing electrolyte conditions, temperature, Pt loading, or support structure may produce different behavior.
Failure of ORR performance to correlate with d-band-center shifts would falsify the hypothesis.
Evidence that performance changes are primarily attributable to strain independently of Ni content would falsify the hypothesis.
